Moved 2026-11-03 from 068f440a. ONE commit, and it is the five reviews finding
four real defects in the emitter the previous revision added.

反向审查 -- a memory-ordering hole. NativeGOPPresenter::start() publishes
native_gop_physical and native_gop_virtual and THEN raises native_gop_ready, with
no barrier on the writer's side and no way for this file to add one there. On
weakly-ordered ARM a reader can observe ready=1 with a stale virtual address. The
read side now takes a dmb ish after seeing the flag and before reading the data;
the native_gop_physical == video.v_baseAddr cross-check is the second line of
defence and fails closed.

性能审查 -- an unbounded work-loop cost. Each arm hashes the whole ~24 MB frame and
a held key delivers a report every 100 ms, so ten reports inside one compare window
were ten hashes. interaction_arm() now returns early if already armed, bounding it
to two hashes per second -- the same order as the registry walk the checkpoint
already does every second.

规范审查 -- memcpy for one aligned copy, replaced with a direct volatile 64-bit load
so the translation unit has no reason to pull in <string.h>.

对质 -- and this one caught a defect introduced WHILE fixing the others. The first
revision of the bounded-copy rewrite carried a parts[] loop that copied all three
literals up front and then copied middle and suffix again after the hex, producing
a record that compiles clean and parses as nothing -- the exact defect two drafts of
the mount emitter had. Caught by reassembling the literals the way the preprocessor
will and parsing the result, which is the only thing that can see it.

That last one is the reason the note exists: the emitter's record was ALREADY valid
when the previous revision was pinned, and the defect appeared in the act of making
the copies safer. A change that improves one property can break another, and the
only detector is the one that reassembles and parses.

The PRD veto is the whole reason it is built the way it is.
milestones.py:1745-1752 refuses a homescreen screenshot plus a mouse click, so
the record cannot mean "input was delivered" -- it has to mean the input changed
what is on screen. Both halves are kernel-side, because the guest userspace is
Apple's real code and cannot be modified to emit anything:

  the screen -- NativeGOPPresenter::start() maps the scanout writable and
    cross-checks it against PE_current_console() (same v_baseAddr, v_width,
    v_height, v_rowBytes, depth 32, no rotate), then publishes native_gop_ready
    and native_gop_virtual. A digest over those bytes is a measurement.
  the input -- native_hid_input_observed() is called on every report the driver
    hands to the HID stack.

Digest, deliver, digest again, report only if the two differ. The compare runs on
the timer's own 1-second cadence.

THE LINKAGE IS SAFE BY CONFIGURATION, and that was established before writing the
code rather than after. This object is force-loaded via libNativeLegacyDisplay.late.a
(build-native-legacy-display.py:252-254, build-xnu-4k-baseline.sh:625-627); the
console archive is force-loaded separately (build-xnu-4k-baseline.sh:672-677). The
only defconfig that sets CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_LEGACY_DISPLAY is qemu_root_defconfig,
and it also sets CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_CONSOLE. qemu_defconfig sets NEITHER. So
there is no configuration in which the strong reference is unresolved, which is
what allows it to be strong -- and a strong reference is what makes a missing
archive fail the link naming the symbol instead of silently dropping the record.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE, recorded here so it is not forgotten later: a digest
changing proves the screen changed after input, not that the user's intent was
honoured. A clock redraw would also change it. The record carries BOTH digests
rather than a boolean. There is deliberately no changed-byte count -- computing
one means holding a second copy of a ~24 MB frame.

A fork of xVanTuring/UniXNU-qemu at the previous pin 73e5154aa455d5f1dcd74f8e66ce4a2a410c4470 plus exactly one commit, which fixes the scanout client's selector search. The bug was two halves and both were quiet. admittedSelector() looped selector = 0..255 and called tunnel(link, kProbe, ...), which read the selector out of link.selector -- the field the loop was trying to fill in -- so every one of the 256 probes asked selector 0 whatever the loop variable said. It then returned 0 on the failure path, and the caller's `if (!link.selector)` read that 0 as "nothing is admitted". A sandbox profile that admits selector 0 is therefore a WORKING hand-off that this code logged as "the profile admits no external-method selector for this class" and never asked the presenter for a frame; native_gop_gpu_offers stays 0, which is exactly what it was before the hand-off existed, so the defect is invisible in the counters. The fix lands both halves together: tunnel() takes the selector as a PARAMETER (a search cannot consult the one field it is filling in), and "nothing is admitted" becomes kNoSelector = 0xffffffff, which selector 0 cannot produce, so the caller compares against it instead of testing the selector for truth. The search moves into QemuMetalSelector.h, a header of plain C++ with no IOKit and no Mach types, so the host's own toolchain can compile and RUN it -- and that is the point, because the bug was invisible to every source-level guard this repository has. A guard reading the broken code sees a loop, a call, a compared return value and a return on the failure path: all four of the shapes it could ask for. Only executing the loop with a probe that admits DIFFERENT selectors separates the two versions. tests/unit/test_qemu_metal_selector.py does that, five cases: selector 0 admitted (expects 0, asked exactly once), only selector 7 (expects 7, asked eight times -- 256 asks of one selector is the bug and this is the case where it shows), nothing admitted (expects kNoSelector, asked 256), selector 255 (reachable, not clipped by a bound of 255), and a null probe (kNoSelector, not a crash). MEASURED on the Windows code-stage host with MSVC 14.30.30705: all five cases pass. MUTATION-TESTED, which is the part that matters: restoring the broken loop form kills 5 of 11 assertions and exits 1, and reintroducing either half in the .mm alone (the truth test, or callFn reading link.selector again) turns the source guard red. Case 1 passes on the mutant too, and that is correct rather than a gap -- the broken code got "selector 0 admitted" right by accident; cases 2 through 5 are what catch it. pinned_checkouts_note: Three repositories are pinned here, and only two of them are in `feeds`. `unixnu` and `device_repo` are the two the driver cannot clone for itself (cli.py has no subcommand that clones either; scripts/unixnu/config.py raises 'no device repository' without -D), so the workflow's acquisition step clones them into vendor/. `uefi_sheng` is NOT a feed on purpose: the driver's feeds.fetch() resolves sources named by a feeds.toml and writes them into out/<board>/feeds, and uefi-sheng is named by no feeds.toml -- it is the Mu-Silicium checkout the driver's --uefi option points at (cli.py:24). Adding it to `feeds` would make the workflow's cross-check demand it in the driver's own unixnu.lock, where it will never appear, and would fail every run. So it is pinned here, acquired by the same step, and verified by the one file the build actually reads (uefi_sheng.font_header.sha256) rather than by a feed pin. Measured on run 40187668943 (stage M4): build-os-root.py reached step 9 for the first time -- storage-abi, both signed policies, the verified-root probe, NativeVirtioBlock/NativeRamBlock verified bindings, the grown 1 GiB OwnerData volume (675761EF-5622-4F5B-89DF-4CAD5BA456F6) and the packed ramdisk all passed -- and then died in build-native-legacy-display.py -> build-arm-driver.py NativeLegacyDisplay with `NativeLegacyDisplay.cpp:206:59: error: only virtual member functions can be marked 'override'` and `:207:13: error: no member named 'getRefreshAttributes' in 'IOMobileFramebufferLegacy'`.
